open_items: Read the cgroup memory limit on the next run to explain why vLLM saw 3.85 GiB available RAM while /proc/meminfo showed 27 GiB
Confirm the prefix-cache counters stay flat over a run (run-level deltas in the manifest)
Why decode tok/s is faster at 1K with graphs on while the GPU clock is lowest there (clock confounder; needs clock-controlled or more samples)
Explain the 20 percent 8K decode slowdown with graphs and the order-independent TTFT stability seen in the sweep
Record the engine scheduler limits (max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs) in the run manifest; they are not in the vLLM 0.34.0 server log
Why greedy outputs diverge at 1K under batching at one text position (character 222) while longer prompts mostly do not
To price the capacity limit separately from serial prefill: a 32K run with a longer output (e.g. 512 tokens) or N above 10, so a request frees blocks later than the serial queue releases
Verify the scheduler token budget (max_num_batched_tokens) directly; the decode-starvation arithmetic assumes 2,048
Check /dev/shm capacity and the largest safe --kv-offloading-size inside the 30 GiB container; record container_shmem_mib (added after the probe)
Explain why the offload run's second request had a 0.058 s first token versus 0.253 s for prefix-only (single observation)
Possible follow-up after the sweep: a shuffled-revisit run (--revisit-order shuffled) and a larger offload buffer, only if memory allows
Optional: add S = 64 and 80 to locate the prefix-cache loss point (about 74 expected), and a shuffled-revisit run for a smoother curve

Investigate why the native CPU offload tier served no hits: minimal evict-then-revisit check recording vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total, other block sizes, release notes and issues for vLLM 0.34 extensible KV cache + OffloadingConnector
Step 9 written findings and acceptance (strategy support matrix: prefix cache active, fp8 unsupported on T4, CPU offload starts but gave no benefit here)

step8_32k.config: 32,000 x N 1/4/8/10, 1 unmeasured warmup wave at N=1, 1 measured wave per cell, enforce_eager OFF, max_model_len 32768, timeout 7200 s
step8_32k.capacity_boundary: one 32K request = 502 blocks; 9 x 502 = 4,518 of 4,831 usable blocks, so a tenth cannot be admitted until a request finishes. Engine timeline for N=10: running rose by one about every 171 s (as each prefill started), reached 9 with 1 waiting at 1,312 s, dropped to 8 at 1,483.5 s when the first request finished, and was 9 with 0 waiting at 1,484.0 s. The cell cannot separate the capacity wait from the serial-prefill wait because both ended at the same moment; a longer output or a larger N would be needed.
step8_32k.decode_starvation: earliest request decodes at 0.25 / 0.11 / 0.10 tok/s at N=4 / 8 / 10 (23.5 alone); latest at 10.0 / 8.2 / 8.4. One token per ~10 s equals one 2,048-token prefill chunk step (163.5 s / 16 chunks = 10.2 s); at 16K the same arithmetic gives 5.6 s per step versus 5.3 s observed. This inference assumes a 2,048-token step budget that the server log does not state.
step8_32k.first_request_finish_time: the first request finished at 1,483.5 s, about 127 steps after its first token, i.e. after roughly eight more 32K prefills
step8_32k.batch_invariance: L32000-000 output at N=4, 8 and 10 is identical but differs from its N=1 output at character 227 of 611; the 1K prompt diverged at character 222 in the same kind of comparison
